title: Weddings, festivals & occasions
goal: Invite and be invited, find your way through a three-day wedding, give the right wishes and blessings, and join in Diwali, Holi, Eid and birthdays.
intro:
Sooner or later someone will tell you **शादी में ज़रूर आना!** — and a north Indian wedding is three days of events, food, dancing and relatives. This unit gives you the names of the events (**मेहंदी, संगीत, बारात, फेरे**), what to give (**शगुन**), and what to say to the couple, the family and the elders who bless you.

You'll also learn the big festivals the way people celebrate them — lamps and sweets at **दीवाली**, colour and chaos at **होली** (**बुरा न मानो, होली है!**), sevaiyan at **ईद** — and the grammar of **wishes and blessings** (**ख़ुश रहो**, **जोड़ी सलामत रहे**) and of **'be sure to…'** (**आना मत भूलना!**).

grammar.title: Wishes and blessings: ख़ुश रहो, ख़ुश रहें, भगवान करे…
grammar.body:
Hindi has a whole grammar for wishing people well, and you'll hear it at every occasion.

**1. X मुबारक हो / X की बधाई हो / X की शुभकामनाएँ.** The **हो** at the end is the **subjunctive** of होना — 'may it be': जन्मदिन मुबारक **हो** 'may your birthday be blessed'. People often drop it: ईद मुबारक!

**2. The subjunctive for 'may…'.** From unit 18: the subjunctive is the future without -गा/-गी/-गे. Use it for any wish:
आप हमेशा ख़ुश **रहें** 'may you always be happy'
जोड़ी सलामत **रहे** 'may the couple stay together'
तुम्हारा हर सपना पूरा **हो** 'may all your dreams come true'

**3. भगवान करे (कि)… / ख़ुदा करे… 'God grant that…'** followed by a subjunctive: भगवान करे, तुम्हें यह नौकरी मिल **जाए**. Also **भगवान तुम्हें** लंबी उम्र **दे** 'may God give you a long life'.

**4. Elders bless with the plain imperative.** When you touch an older relative's feet they say **ख़ुश रहो**, **जुग-जुग जियो** 'live for ages', **सदा सुखी रहो** 'always be content' — imperatives used as blessings. To a bride, older women say **सदा सुहागन रहो**. You don't bless elders back; you thank them or just smile.

**The trap:** a wish is not a prediction. आप ख़ुश **रहेंगे** means 'you will be happy' (a forecast). For 'may you be happy' use the subjunctive **रहें**. And the subjunctive agrees with its subject: जोड़ी (f) सलामत **रहे**, आप दोनों सलामत **रहें**.

The standard reply to any wish is **आपको भी!** 'you too!' (or **सेम टू यू**), and to **ईद मुबारक**, **ख़ैर मुबारक**.

grammar.title: 'Be sure to…', 'don't forget to…': ज़रूर आना, आना मत भूलना
grammar.body:
Invitations come with insistence. Three tools:

**1. The infinitive as a 'later' command.** With तुम, the dictionary form (**आना, बताना, फ़ोन करना**) works as a friendly request for some time in the future: कल **आना** 'come tomorrow', पहुँचकर **बताना** 'let me know when you get there'. It sounds softer and more caring than आओ. The polite equivalent with आप is **-इएगा**: **आइएगा, बताइएगा**.

**2. ज़रूर 'definitely'.** Put it before the verb, or after it for extra push: शादी में **ज़रूर आना** · आना **ज़रूर**! · **पक्का** आना 'come for sure'. **ज़रूर से ज़रूर** is the strongest form.

**3. 'Don't forget to…' = infinitive + मत भूलना.** आना **मत भूलना** 'don't forget to come', केक लाना **मत भूलना** 'don't forget to bring the cake'. Word order is flexible: **भूलना मत**.

And the host's famous insistence: **खाना खाकर जाना** 'eat before you go' — the **-कर** form (unit 16) + जाना.

To **accept**: ज़रूर आएँगे! / पक्का! / **हम ज़रूर आएँगे**. To **decline politely**, never a bare no: **कोशिश करूँगा** 'I'll try', or give a reason and your wishes: **नहीं आ पाऊँगी, पर मेरी तरफ़ से बहुत-बहुत बधाई**.

**The trap:** with the infinitive command, the negative is **मत** (or न), not नहीं: भूलना **मत**, never भूलना नहीं as a request.

culture:
**Wedding season** in north India runs roughly from November to February, and invitations arrive as heavy printed cards, often with a box of sweets, followed by a WhatsApp e-card. 'Come to the wedding' is meant literally: friends of friends, colleagues and neighbours are all welcome, and a guest list of 500 is ordinary. Wear bright colours; avoid all-white (associated with mourning) and all-black at a Hindu wedding. Give **शगुन** in an envelope — always an odd sum ending in 1 — and hand it to the couple on stage, where you'll also be photographed. Muslim weddings have the **निकाह** and the **वलीमा** reception; Sikh weddings the **आनंद कारज** in the gurdwara, with heads covered.

Touching elders' **feet** (or bending towards them) at weddings and festivals is normal even for young city people; the elder blesses you with **ख़ुश रहो** or **जुग-जुग जियो**. At **Diwali** people clean and decorate the house, light **दिए**, draw **रंगोली**, visit friends with boxes of sweets or dry fruit and play cards; many cities now restrict crackers because of air pollution. **Holi** is loud, wet and colourful: wear old clothes, and expect strangers to colour you with **बुरा न मानो, होली है!** At **Eid** families visit each other for **सेवइयाँ** and biryani, and children collect **ईदी** (gift money). In Bihar and eastern UP the biggest festival is **छठ**. Birthdays are cake, a treat for friends, and a flood of **HBD** messages.

tip.title: ज़रूर आना — be sure to come
tip.body:
- With तुम, the infinitive is a friendly 'later' request: कल **आना**, फ़ोन **करना**. Polite: **आइएगा**.
- **ज़रूर** or **पक्का** adds 'for sure': ज़रूर आना, पक्का आना.
- 'Don't forget to…' = infinitive + **मत भूलना**: आना मत भूलना.
- The negative is **मत**, not नहीं.

tip.title: The events of a north Indian wedding
tip.body:
- **सगाई** engagement → **मेहंदी** henna night → **संगीत** dance night → **बारात** the groom's procession → **फेरे** the ceremony → **रिसेप्शन** the party.
- बारात is feminine: बारात **आएगी**. फेरे is plural: फेरे **हुए**.
- Compliments: दुल्हन बहुत सुंदर **लग रही है**.

tip.title: May you…: the subjunctive of wishes
tip.body:
- Wishes use the **subjunctive**: आप ख़ुश **रहें**, जोड़ी सलामत **रहे**, सपना पूरा **हो**.
- **X मुबारक हो**, **X की बधाई हो** — that हो means 'may it be'.
- **भगवान करे…** 'God grant…' + subjunctive: नौकरी मिल **जाए**.
- Elders bless with the imperative: **ख़ुश रहो**, **जुग-जुग जियो**.
tip.pattern: आप ख़ुश रहें  ·  भगवान करे + subjunctive

sentences.native: भगवान करे, तुम्हें यह नौकरी मिल जाए।
sentences.roman: bhagvān kare, tumheṃ yah naukrī mil jāe.
sentences.en: I really hope you get this job.

sentences.native: आप हमेशा ख़ुश रहें।
sentences.roman: āp hameshā xush raheṃ.
sentences.en: May you always be happy.

sentences.native: आप दोनों को बहुत-बहुत बधाई! जोड़ी सलामत रहे!
sentences.roman: āp donoṃ ko bahut-bahut badhāī! joṛī salāmat rahe!
sentences.en: Many congratulations to you both! May you always be together!

sentences.native: जुग-जुग जियो! भगवान तुम्हें लंबी उम्र दे।
sentences.roman: jug-jug jiyo! bhagvān tumheṃ lambī umr de.
sentences.en: Live long! May God give you a long life.

sentences.native: तुम्हारा हर सपना पूरा हो!
sentences.roman: tumhārā har sapnā pūrā ho!
sentences.en: May all your dreams come true!

sentences.native: मैंने दादी के पैर छुए और उन्होंने कहा, ख़ुश रहो।
sentences.roman: maiṃne dādī ke pair chhue aur unhoṃne kahā, xush raho.
sentences.en: I touched Grandma's feet and she said, 'Bless you.'

sentences.native: बड़ों के पैर छूना मत भूलना।
sentences.roman: baṛoṃ ke pair chhūnā mat bhūlnā.
sentences.en: Don't forget to touch the elders' feet.

sentences.native: क्या जोड़ी है! दोनों बहुत अच्छे लग रहे हैं।
sentences.roman: kyā joṛī hai! donoṃ bahut achchhe lag rahe haiṃ.
sentences.en: What a couple! They both look great.

sentences.native: आज मेरा जन्मदिन है, और किसी को याद नहीं!
sentences.roman: āj merā janmdin hai, aur kisī ko yād nahīṃ!
sentences.en: It's my birthday today and nobody remembers!

lessons.title: Gifts and anniversaries

tip.title: Giving and receiving gifts
tip.body:
- At weddings most people give **शगुन**: cash in a **लिफ़ाफ़ा**, always an odd sum (₹101, ₹501).
- Hand it over modestly: **हमारी तरफ़ से एक छोटा-सा तोहफ़ा**.
- Receiving, protest a little: **अरे, इसकी क्या ज़रूरत थी?** 'oh, you shouldn't have!'
- Gifts are often not opened in front of the giver.

new: हमारी तरफ़ से एक छोटा-सा तोहफ़ा।

sentences.native: शगुन में कितने पैसे देते हैं?
sentences.roman: shagun meṃ kitne paise dete haiṃ?
sentences.en: How much money do people give as shagun?

sentences.native: लिफ़ाफ़े में पाँच सौ एक रुपये रख दो।
sentences.roman: lifāfe meṃ pāṃch sau ek rupaye rakh do.
sentences.en: Put five hundred and one rupees in the envelope.

sentences.native: अरे, इसकी क्या ज़रूरत थी?
sentences.roman: are, iskī kyā zarūrat thī?
sentences.en: Oh, you really shouldn't have!

sentences.native: हमारी तरफ़ से एक छोटा-सा तोहफ़ा, आपकी सालगिरह के लिए।
sentences.roman: hamārī taraf se ek chhoṭā-sā tohfā, āpkī sālgirah ke liye.
sentences.en: A little something from us, for your anniversary.

sentences.native: आज माँ और पापा की शादी की सालगिरह है।
sentences.roman: āj māṃ aur pāpā kī shādī kī sālgirah hai.
sentences.en: It's Mum and Dad's wedding anniversary today.

sentences.native: शादी की सालगिरह मुबारक! आप दोनों हमेशा ऐसे ही रहें।
sentences.roman: shādī kī sālgirah mubārak! āp donoṃ hameshā aise hī raheṃ.
sentences.en: Happy anniversary! May you two always stay just like this.

sentences.native: शगुन हमेशा एक सौ एक या पाँच सौ एक का होता है।
sentences.roman: shagun hameshā ek sau ek yā pāṃch sau ek kā hotā hai.
sentences.en: Shagun is always 101 or 501.

sentences.native: उसके जन्मदिन के लिए क्या तोहफ़ा लें?
sentences.roman: uske janmdin ke liye kyā tohfā leṃ?
sentences.en: What shall we get her for her birthday?

sentences.native: दीवाली की बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएँ, आपको और आपके परिवार को!
sentences.roman: dīvālī kī bahut-bahut shubhkāmnāeṃ, āpko aur āpke parivār ko!
sentences.en: Happy Diwali to you and your family!

sentences.native: हमने पूरा घर दियों से सजाया।
sentences.roman: hamne pūrā ghar diyoṃ se sajāyā.
sentences.en: We decorated the whole house with lamps.

sentences.native: दिए कितने सुंदर लग रहे हैं!
sentences.roman: diye kitne sundar lag rahe haiṃ!
sentences.en: The lamps look so beautiful!

sentences.native: इस बार हम पटाखे नहीं ख़रीदेंगे।
sentences.roman: is bār ham paṭākhe nahīṃ xarīdeṃge.
sentences.en: We're not buying crackers this time.

sentences.native: दीवाली पर सब एक-दूसरे को मिठाई देते हैं।
sentences.roman: dīvālī par sab ek-dūsre ko miṭhāī dete haiṃ.
sentences.en: At Diwali everyone gives each other sweets.

sentences.native: दीवाली से पहले हम घर साफ़ करते हैं और सजाते हैं।
sentences.roman: dīvālī se pahle ham ghar sāf karte haiṃ aur sajāte haiṃ.
sentences.en: Before Diwali we clean and decorate the house.

sentences.native: बाहर रंगोली किसने बनाई? बहुत सुंदर है!
sentences.roman: bāhar raṅgolī kisne banāī? bahut sundar hai!
sentences.en: Who made the rangoli outside? It's beautiful!

sentences.native: राखी पर मैं अपनी बहन से मिलने जाऊँगा।
sentences.roman: rākhī par maiṃ apnī bahan se milne jāūṃgā.
sentences.en: I'm going to see my sister for Rakhi.

sentences.native: आपको भी दीवाली की शुभकामनाएँ!
sentences.roman: āpko bhī dīvālī kī shubhkāmnāeṃ!
sentences.en: Happy Diwali to you too!

sentences.native: बुरा न मानो, होली है! थोड़ा गुलाल तो लगाना पड़ेगा।
sentences.roman: burā na māno, holī hai! thoṛā gulāl to lagānā paṛegā.
sentences.en: Don't be offended, it's Holi! You've got to have a bit of colour.

sentences.native: होली पर पुराने कपड़े पहनना, रंग नहीं जाता।
sentences.roman: holī par purāne kapṛe pahannā, raṅg nahīṃ jātā.
sentences.en: Wear old clothes for Holi — the colour doesn't come out.

sentences.native: होली है! सबको रंग लगाओ!
sentences.roman: holī hai! sabko raṅg lagāo!
sentences.en: It's Holi! Put colour on everyone!

sentences.native: कल कितने बजे रंग खेलेंगे?
sentences.roman: kal kitne baje raṅg kheleṃge?
sentences.en: What time are we playing Holi tomorrow?

sentences.native: पिछली होली पर मैं पूरा हरा हो गया था!
sentences.roman: pichhlī holī par maiṃ pūrā harā ho gayā thā!
sentences.en: Last Holi I turned completely green!

sentences.native: ईद मुबारक! सेवइयाँ खाने ज़रूर आना।
sentences.roman: īd mubārak! sevaiyāṃ khāne zarūr ānā.
sentences.en: Eid Mubarak! Be sure to come over for sevaiyan.

sentences.native: आंटी ने बहुत अच्छी सेवइयाँ बनाई हैं।
sentences.roman: āṇṭī ne bahut achchhī sevaiyāṃ banāī haiṃ.
sentences.en: Auntie's made really good sevaiyan.

sentences.native: आपको भी ईद मुबारक!
sentences.roman: āpko bhī īd mubārak!
sentences.en: Eid Mubarak to you too!

sentences.native: ईद पर हम सब दोस्तों के घर गए।
sentences.roman: īd par ham sab dostoṃ ke ghar gaye.
sentences.en: On Eid we all went round to our friends' houses.
